title: Field-Multiplier Security of POET
summary: A distinguishing attack applies when POET uses a uniform-random-involution AXU hash; whether its online-encryption theorem remains valid with a field multiplier, and if so how to reprove it, is open.

formal_statement.body: A distinguishing attack against POET is described when its AXU hash is instantiated as a uniform random involution, while it is conjectured that POET's claimed online-encryption security theorem may remain valid when the AXU hash is instantiated as a field multiplier. The unresolved task is to establish whether the theorem remains valid under the field-multiplier instantiation and, if so, provide a revised proof or reduction.

scope.domain: Authenticated-encryption security proofs for POET under different AXU-hash instantiations.
parameters: AXU-hash instantiation — uniform random involution for the attacked variant and field multiplier for the conjectured variant
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish whether POET's claimed online-encryption security theorem remains valid with the field-multiplier instantiation and, if so, provide a revised proof or reduction.

citations.label: Forging Attacks on Two Authenticated Encryption Schemes COBRA and POET

progress.summary: The source gives a single-query, nonce-respecting distinguishing privacy attack for the uniform-random-involution instantiation. It states that the theorem is believed to remain valid with the field-multiplier instantiation, but that the proof must be revised.
citation_labels: Mridul Nandi et al., Forging Attacks on Two Authenticated Encryption Schemes COBRA and POET
